notes:
Sales notes — RAG / embeddings + rerank for product search (focused on cost-per-query and seasonal spikes):
- Customer profile: mid/enterprise DTC retail marketplace, heavy catalog (current ~1.2M SKUs; target ~8M). Global storefronts, localized content.
- Primary ask: semantic search + product reranking that keeps average query cost low during normal ops and scales for 8-10x Black Friday spikes. Wants predictable unit economics.
- Performance targets: p95 retrieval <120ms, full pipeline (retrieve + rerank) p95 <300ms; acceptable p99 for rerank <=600ms for complex queries.
- Cost sensitivity: goal ~<$0.01 per full query (embed + ANN + cross-encoder rerank); currently paying ~$0.018/query with incumbent. Asking for cost model for 1M, 4M, 8M SKU states.
- Rerank approach: prefer two-stage pipeline — cheap embedding retrieve (ANN) + lightweight re-ranker in most cases; cross-encoder fallback for top-10 on high-value queries. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization to reduce costs.
- Indexing concerns: bulk import throughput (can they seed 8M SKUs in a 48-72h migration window?), incremental update latency for price/stock updates (<2 min desired).
- Data controls: must support VPC/private control plane, KMS integration, SSO for admin UI, audit logs retention 12 months, EU data residency for EU storefronts.
- Quote from Head of Search: "We need search to be both better and cheaper — seasonal peaks kill our margin today."
- POC notes: sample index used 150k SKUs, vector dim 768, ANN recall 0.88@100, rerank improved top-10 click-through +18%. Cost analysis run on POC instance attached (drive:/decks/veridian-redwood-poc.pdf).
- Risk areas: rerank CPU cost under peak; candidate fallback model for capacity-constrained windows; cache hit rate for repeated queries.
- Ask from AE: provide a Dedicated capacity proposal (reserved pool + burst) and hosted fallback plan; include pricing for quantized embeddings and pinned model variants.
- Next: Extended POC simulating 8M index (synthetic data) — Redwood to provide an estimated cost-per-query matrix and recommendations by 2026-03-25.
- Jira escalation: REDW-1123 opened for infra questions (index throughput, shard sizing).
